analysis.one_liner: Hitachi Energy India (formerly ABB Power Products and Systems India) makes power transmission and grid equipment - large transformers, HVDC systems, high-voltage switchgear and grid-automation software - sold mainly to Power Grid Corporation and other utilities building out India's electricity grid.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026) were reported on 12 November 2026: revenue rose 63.5% YoY to ₹2,996.5 crore, order inflow jumped 85.9% YoY to ₹4,120.8 crore, and the order backlog hit a record ₹33,335 crore. PAT grew a slower 20.5% YoY to ₹318.5 crore because operating margins narrowed. The stock rallied sharply the next trading day but remains well below its May 2026 peak. The next quarterly results (Q3 FY27) are expected around early-to-mid February 2027, not imminent.
analysis.plain_terms: This is India's grid-equipment boom playing out in a single stock: orders and revenue are growing very fast because utilities are buying transformers and HVDC lines to upgrade the power grid. But the business is making slightly less profit on every rupee of sales than it was a year ago, and the market had already priced in years of growth before this quarter's results. So you have a company genuinely doing more business, trading at a price that assumes it keeps doing even more, while profitability per rupee is actually softening a touch.
analysis.quarters: Revenue growth has accelerated through FY27 (Q1 FY27 revenue ~₹2,494cr, Q2 FY27 ₹2,996.5cr, both well above year-ago quarters), and order backlog has climbed steadily from ₹29,555cr (March 2026) to ₹29,872cr (Dec 2025 quarter) to ₹32,222cr (June 2026) to ₹33,335cr (Sept 2026). But operating margin (excluding other income) fell to about 13.9% in Q2 FY27 from roughly 14.9% the prior quarter and about 17.0% a year earlier - management's own release flags rising employee costs and a higher effective tax rate (26.0% vs 24.5%) as drivers. The quarter also carried a non-cash, timing-related foreign-exchange and commodity-derivative loss of about ₹88 crore, which the company itself called out separately - this is not a core operating item and should not be read as a trading loss. Management's commentary centred on transmission and data-centre-linked orders, and exports (up 184% YoY in H1 FY27) as a new growth leg.
analysis.performance_read: There is no stock split or demerger in this company's history, so the price series is clean and the return figures are not an artefact of corporate actions. On that basis, the long-run numbers are genuinely exceptional: roughly 1,148% over 5 years and 623% over 3 years, both far ahead of the Nifty and of peer ABB India. The last 3 months (-11.5%) and the 17.8% pullback from the May 2026 peak of ₹38,435.82 are real price declines, not statistical distortions - they reflect profit-booking and valuation concerns after an extraordinary run, not any operational setback.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades at roughly 115-120x trailing earnings and about 24.5x book value - a large premium even against other expensive capital-goods names (one analysis put the peer median P/E near 36x). Why it is expensive is clear: near-30% ROCE, a record and growing order book, a net-cash balance sheet, and a multi-year grid-capex and HVDC theme that some analysts describe as having visibility out to 2035. Whether that is a fair price is a separate question - at this multiple, the market is already paying for several years of continued order growth and margin recovery, so even a strong quarter (as this one was on revenue and orders) can disappoint if margins keep slipping, which is arguably what has been happening.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is volume-led, not margin-led: revenue and order inflow are both growing strongly (63.5% and 85.9% YoY respectively), and the backlog keeps hitting new records. But this volume growth is currently diluting margins rather than reinforcing them - operating margin has fallen for two straight comparisons (QoQ and YoY) as employee costs and tax outpaced revenue. That is the opposite problem to the usual commodity-business pattern (flat volumes, rising margin) and is worth tracking: strong volume growth is only durable here if margins stabilise as the backlog converts to revenue.
analysis.health_read: The company is effectively debt-free with negligible interest costs (about ₹2.6 crore in the quarter), and ROE (~22%) and ROCE (~29%) are both strong, so financial risk looks low. Whether profits are converting cleanly to cash (operating cash flow, working capital tied up in long-dated project execution) is not verified here - check on Screener. The more relevant risk for this business is execution risk: a record backlog has to be delivered on time and at acceptable margins, and a new ₹2,000 crore transformer plant at Vadodara (part of a cumulative ~₹4,000 crore capacity programme) is not expected to be ready until around Q4 calendar 2028, so near-term capacity constraints could affect how fast the backlog converts to revenue.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter, Hitachi Energy Ltd (the Hitachi group), holds 71.31% as of September 2026, unchanged since March 2025 after stepping down from 75% in an earlier stake sale - no pledging was found anywhere in the available filings, consistent with a clean, debt-free profile. FII holding was trimmed slightly, from 12.44% to 11.96% quarter-on-quarter, alongside the recent price pullback. DII holding is a modest 6.54% and public holding 10.19%. No marquee individual or well-known domestic investor was found on the shareholder register in the sources checked - if a famous investor name is expected here, it is not currently visible in the data.
strengths: Record order backlog of ₹33,335 crore (Sept 2026), up from ₹29,555 crore in March 2026
Revenue up 63.5% YoY and order inflow up 85.9% YoY in the September 2026 quarter
Net-cash balance sheet with ROCE near 29% and negligible interest cost (~₹2.6 crore/quarter)
Exports up 184% YoY in H1 FY27, giving a growth driver outside the domestic capex cycle
watchpoints: Operating margin (ex-other income) has fallen from about 17.0% a year ago to about 13.9% this quarter, driven by rising employee costs and a higher tax rate
Trading at roughly 115-120x trailing earnings and ~24.5x book value, several times the capital-goods peer median - leaves little room for disappointment
Stock is down 17.8% from its May 2026 peak and FII holding was trimmed from 12.44% to 11.96% quarter-on-quarter
New ₹2,000 crore Vadodara transformer capacity not due until around Q4 CY2028, creating a lag between order backlog growth and the capacity to deliver it
analysis.one_thing: Whether operating margin stabilises or keeps declining in the next couple of quarters (Q3 FY27, expected around February 2027) - a margin recovery would support the case that strong order growth is translating into durable profit growth; continued margin erosion alongside a near-120x earnings multiple would be the clearer warning sign.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly P&L and order/backlog figures are cross-checked against the company's own 12 November 2026 press release and are consistent with Screener.in. Shareholding figures use Screener.in's September 2026 breakup (71.31/11.96/6.54/10.19, which sums cleanly to 100%); a conflicting shareholding snapshot found elsewhere did not sum correctly and was discarded as unreliable. Current valuation multiples (P/E ~113-119x, P/B 24.5x, ROE ~22%, ROCE ~29%) are reasonably consistent across sources, but historical average P/E figures varied widely (116x to 206x depending on source and period) and are not comparable enough to report as a single number, so they have been omitted. Price, return and drawdown figures are taken as given and not independently recomputed; no stock split or demerger affects this series. Cash-flow conversion (operating cash flow vs reported profit) was not verified - check on Screener.
